html:
Guachimis is the map's label for peoples of the northern half of the Baja California peninsula, in Mexico. The name is not in the usual sources.

In the 1500s this dry land was home to small bands of hunter-gatherers, among them the Cochimí and, further north, the Kiliwa and Paipai. They lived on seeds, agave, cactus fruit, small game and shellfish, moving between water holes. Jesuit missions reached the area in the 1700s, and the epidemics that followed killed most of the people, as in other desert foraging lands.
